features.name: production background
features.description: This captures how much directly relevant software engineering experience the letter presents, scored by the duration and scope of production service testing, maintenance, and launches it describes.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.evidence: Bachelor's degree ... Master's degree ... Doctoral degree
features.name: academic credential
features.description: This captures the highest formal academic preparation the letter presents in a relevant technical field.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree, equivalent, or no advanced degree is presented.
Master's degree is presented.
Doctoral degree is presented.

features.evidence: typed, tested services and tooling that other engineers extend without fear
features.name: Python depth
features.description: This captures how convincingly the letter establishes Python as a production language the applicant actively uses.

levels.descriptor: Python is not mentioned.
Python is mentioned, but only as a general tool or scripting language.
Python is clearly used regularly for services, tooling, or automation.
Python is presented as production-grade work, with specifics such as typed or tested services, shared tooling, or major automation ownership.

features.evidence: shipping model-integrated functionality wrapped in the checks that make it dependable
features.name: AI reliability experience
features.description: This captures how much real-world AI experience the letter shows, scored by whether it moves from generic model exposure to production deployment with reliability controls.

levels.descriptor: No AI or LLM experience is mentioned.
AI experience is mentioned only generically, with little sign of real deployment.
The letter shows direct production AI work, such as shipping model-backed features.
The letter shows production AI work plus explicit attention to evaluation, trustworthiness, guardrails, or failure modes.

features.evidence: Python agents ... Go services define their permissions and audit their actions
features.name: agentic design depth
features.description: This captures how concretely the letter explains agentic-system design, especially bounded autonomy, interfaces, supervision, and auditability.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or agent-based system design is mentioned.
Agents are mentioned, but the architecture or controls are vague.
The letter clearly describes a Python-agent and Go-backend pattern or similar role-relevant split.
The letter gives a strong architectural account of bounded autonomy, contracts, permissions, logging, or auditable guardrails.

features.evidence: turned an unstructured queue into a routed, prioritized pipeline
features.name: triage automation ownership
features.description: This captures direct ownership of automating vulnerability intake or triage workflows, scored by whether the letter shows hands-on delivery and operational effect.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability handling or triage automation experience is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in reducing manual security workload, but gives no direct example.
The letter states direct experience automating vulnerability reports or triage workflows.
The letter describes a concrete triage pipeline, classification or routing logic, or clear operational impact from the automation.

features.name: security review practice
features.description: This captures hands-on security assessment experience, scored by whether the letter shows actual review work such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or fix validation.

levels.descriptor: No direct security assessment work is shown.
Security interest or exposure is implied, but actual assessment practice is not established.
The letter clearly states real assessment work such as threat modeling, reviews, or security assessments.
The letter shows a thoughtful or multi-part assessment practice, such as reading code like an attacker, probing design assumptions, or validating fixes.

features.evidence: turned a brute-force correlation job into a streaming computation
features.name: algorithmic fluency
features.description: This captures evidence of strong data-structure or algorithmic problem solving through concrete redesign or optimization examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
The letter claims algorithmic strength, but gives no real example.
The letter gives one concrete example of an algorithmic improvement or redesign.
The letter shows especially strong algorithmic sophistication by reframing a hard problem into a clearly better structure or approach.

features.evidence: scale scarce security judgment across an entire company
features.name: leverage framing
features.description: This captures how clearly the letter understands the role as high-leverage security automation for foundational infrastructure rather than generic software work.

levels.descriptor: Interest is generic and does not show much understanding of the team's leverage.
The letter mentions scale or security broadly, but the framing remains general.
The letter clearly frames the role as central security automation or capacity multiplication.
The letter shows nuanced understanding of leverage points such as foundational tooling, triage, variant analysis, or fleet-wide impact.

features.evidence: make the secure path the easy path
features.name: developer enablement
features.description: This captures whether the letter frames security tooling as helping developer teams adopt better defaults with less friction.

levels.descriptor: No developer-enablement mindset is visible.
The letter shows a general desire to help teams, but not much more.
The letter explicitly talks about secure defaults, user proximity, or removing friction for developers.
The letter repeatedly centers developer workflow improvement and treats success as making secure behavior easier than insecure behavior.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned to the team
features.name: evidence specificity
features.description: This captures how much the letter backs claims with concrete examples, quantities, outcomes, or named artifacts rather than generic self-description.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on unsupported assertions or broad adjectives.
Some specifics appear, but evidence remains sparse or outcomes are unclear.
Several concrete examples, counts, or project details support the claims.
Multiple concrete achievements are tied to clear outcomes, impact, or memorable technical artifacts.

features.name: proofreading quality
features.description: This captures the degree of mechanical polish, scored by the frequency and distractiveness of spelling, grammar, or typographical errors.

levels.descriptor: Frequent distracting errors materially hurt readability.
Noticeable errors are present, but the letter remains readable.
Only minor slips appear and they do not strongly distract.
The letter is polished and essentially error-free.

features.evidence: The role reads like the natural continuation of that arc
features.name: narrative cohesion
features.description: This captures how well the letter forms a coherent case for fit, scored by the clarity of its progression from motivation to evidence to role alignment.

levels.descriptor: The letter feels fragmented, list-like, or weakly connected.
The overall point is understandable, but transitions or structure are uneven.
The letter makes a coherent and purposeful case for fit.
The letter is especially crisp, well-shaped, and memorable as an argument.

features.name: security certification
features.description: This captures whether the letter presents formal security certification and how demanding that certification appears.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline security certification such as Security+ is mentioned.
A more advanced practical certification such as OSCP is mentioned.

features.evidence: near-top finishes in several large competitions
features.name: offensive practice
features.description: This captures ongoing offensive-security practice outside routine job duties, especially through capture-the-flag participation with evidence of seriousness.

levels.descriptor: No adversarial practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions CTFs or similar practice casually or without performance signals.
The letter shows sustained or high-performing adversarial practice, such as regular participation or strong placements.

features.evidence: reviewing every contribution and cutting careful releases
features.name: open-source stewardship
features.description: This captures engagement with open-source software, scored from no mention through one-off patches to real project maintenance responsibility.

levels.descriptor: No open-source work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or isolated contributions.
The letter shows repeated or meaningful contribution to open-source tools it uses or depends on.
The letter shows maintainer-level ownership, such as reviews, releases, roadmap direction, or community responsibility.

features.name: project ambition
features.description: This captures the technical ambition of self-directed projects, scored by whether side work is trivial, moderately substantial, or tackles serious systems problems such as distribution, recovery, or consistency.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned, or only a very small utility or app appears.
A modest side project is mentioned, but it shows limited technical stretch.
A substantial side project is described with meaningful engineering decisions or systems design.
An ambitious systems project is described that tackles hard infrastructure concerns such as failover, consensus, recovery, or exactly-once behavior.
